finding: ApplyDamageToCard saves lethality before spill/deal callbacks, then calls before-destroy and removal without a fresh availability gate. Simulator routed this through legacy Destroy, which skipped retained Discard/NotAvailable victims and their death hooks.
authoritative_sequence: ApplyDamageToCard i1304..1379 saves lethality; i1431 notifies, i1699 spills, i1808 deals callbacks; i1861 tests saved flag.
HQ identity branches use cached toCardID and stored side HQ identity; non-HQ branch i2015 before-destroy then i2049 ApplyRemoveCardFromBoard.
Before-destroy fetches victim/attacker, runs own unsuppressed callback then T15 query; no new location gate.
Removal has positive ID gate, fetches current old location, invokes leave/move/after-leave/destruction with no availability or repeated-removal gate.
changes: Add damage-specific internal destroy adapter without legacy availability guard or explicit destroy notification.
Route only saved-lethal non-HQ ApplyDamageToCard removal to that adapter; keep ordinary Destroy behavior.

validation.focused_before: 1 failed / 1 passed on old production; failure first occurs for callback moving victim to Discard

scenarios: Both sides, suppressed/unsuppressed, post-damage heal and board/Discard/NotAvailable/Hand moves, plus nested explicit destruction followed by saved-lethal removal.
Observe before/self/after death counts, retained identity, fresh removal location, repeated history and absence of extra explicit destroy notice.
Nonlethal snapshot does not become lethal when deal callback sets defense to0.
remaining: Scoped to valid positive-ID retained non-HQ objects and normal action processing; missing/nonpositive IDs, object replacement and UObject lifetime are not certified.
Client identifies HQ by stored GameState HQ IDs/references, while simulator still uses type/owner-derived lookup; identity mutation cases remain open.
No whole combat, batch damage, global trigger ordering or individual card death-hook semantics certification.

New tests perturb shared callback state using synthetic IR probes; they do not establish that every perturbation is reachable from a current legal card combination. Existing actual-card IR regressions remain separate.
